targets.text: league-of-agents.ai/evals/ shows model-vs-model matches live, turn by turn, with each model's thinking alongside the board — redesigned, Playwright-verified, and exercised by a pi agent on Nemotron Super
/evals/ on league-of-agents.ai shows a live match advancing turn by turn, its seats' reasoning, Playwright evidence at 1440 and 390 px, and a recorded pi + Nemotron Super run

A data export contract for evals: the prototype builder's data.json (per turn: state, per-side fog vis/seen bitstrings, plans, messages, actions, rejected, latency, think token counts) becomes a versioned schema under league_site/datasets, alongside schema.py/export.py
One versioned schema (league_site/datasets) describes data.json and the thinking files; the page and the exporter both validate against it
GLM reasoning is fetched on demand per seat per turn and runs through league_site/datasets/scrub.py plus a hostname/IP/path check; a failed scrub drops that file, not the turn
No published thinking file contains a hostname, IP address, internal path or credential, and a file that fails the scrub is left out while the turn still publishes
The replay page labels the reasoning asymmetry: GLM full text, Claude seats (claude -p) token counts only — think[].has_text=false and completion_tokens=null for red seats in the data
A reader can tell from the page alone which seats have full reasoning and which have none, and why
Live = fresh static files: the page polls data.json about once a minute, advances only when the viewer sits at the latest turn, and shows a live badge with turn N of limit and updated time
A viewer at the latest turn sees a new turn within about a minute of the export landing, and a viewer scrubbed back is never moved
The redesign reuses the dawn-arena theme tokens from league_site/web/theme.py (Fraunces + Albert Sans, aurora teal accent, light/dark) instead of the prototype's own palette and Chakra Petch fonts
The evals pages use only theme.py tokens and the family fonts, and pass the family-kinship read in light and dark
Each replay header and the index carry the fairness log: void/tie/live status and the harness-bug reason per match (thief-a void, a4 tie, a5 tie, a6 live, opus-a queued)
Every stopped, void or tie match carries a structured status and reason in the export, shown in its header and the index
The engine and harness stay in agentculture/league-of-agents; the platform only consumes exported logs — no harness code is vendored here
No harness or engine code is copied into this repo; the platform imports only exported files

Playwright checks the evals pages at 1440 and 390 px in light and dark: keyboard scrubbing, labelled controls (#36), live-advance not stealing a scrubbing viewer, and the thinking drawer loading on demand
Playwright covers 1440 and 390 px in light and dark, keyboard turn stepping, labelled controls, live advance, and on-demand reasoning loading, and runs in CI
Gameplay sits next to the board it explains: plans, chat, orders and reasoning for a moment are shown beside that moment's board, never in a log section below it
At every width the selected moment's talk is visible together with its board, with no scrolling between them (sticky board on desktop, sticky compact board on phone)
The game is read in slices: the replay breaks a match into key moments, each a board snapshot plus the information drawn from it (what changed, who scored, what the seats said and reasoned about it)
Every slice cites the turn it came from and opens to that turn's full record; nothing on a slice comes from anywhere but the exported data
Agent builders and model evaluators comparing how models play, plus curious visitors following a live match
The page answers both audiences: an evaluator can compare the models from the benchmarks section, a visitor can follow the live match from the story
The prototype replay shows the board, then a score chart, then a full log far below it: you scrub a slider and read a wall of turn records to work out what happened
The before state is the prototype artifact as of 2026-11-08 (board, chart, then log below)
A benchmark result is only credible if a reader can see why it happened: which moments decided the match and what each model was thinking at that moment
Each headline result on the page links to the moments and data that produced it
A reader opens a replay and reads the match as a short story of key moments, each beside its board, and can open any moment to read the orders, chat and GLM reasoning behind it
From any replay, a reader can open any moment and see its orders, chat and GLM reasoning without leaving the board

Slices are derived deterministically from the turn data, not written by hand: a turn becomes a slice when the score changes, a point is captured, a mission completes, a steal happens, a Crown streak starts or ends, the lead changes, or orders are rejected or lost; quiet turns fold into the preceding slice
Running the slicer twice on the same data.json gives identical slices; it is a pure function of the export
Each eval shows a few findings drawn from the slices with their counts, such as rejected orders per side, lost orders, and turns where both sides scored the same on the mirrored board
Each finding links to the slices that back it, so a reader can check the count
Slice headlines are templated from events (team, action, object, points); no LLM writes or summarises match narrative on the site
No text on the evals pages is generated by a model at build or view time; headlines come from templates over events
Someone who has not seen a match can say from the story alone which turns decided it and why, for example hard-a turns 17, 18 and 23, without opening the turn log
Two people who have not seen hard-a both name turns 17, 18 and 23 as deciding moments from the story alone

The evals index carries a benchmarks section computed from the export: chat words per turn, answer time, illegal-order rate and thinking tokens per side; aggression (share of unit-turns in the enemy half, contact within 2 cells) against effectiveness (points per turn); order mix by type; per-match small multiples; GLM thinking tokens per turn. Every chart has hover tooltips, keyboard access and a table view
Each metric is defined in one place, computed only from data.json, and its definition is stated on the page; team colours pass the dataviz palette validator in light and dark

The reasoning and chat scanner fails closed: any text it cannot classify as clean (secret-like strings, hostnames, IPs, absolute paths, emails) keeps that file out of the publish and logs which pattern hit
Running the scanner over all 45 existing thinking files reports every hit with file, seat and pattern, and nothing with a hit is uploaded

Live files are served with explicit cache headers: a running match's data.json at max-age of 30 s or less, finished matches and thinking files immutable; the prior theme.css incident shows Cloudflare holding origin files for 4 hours
curl -I on a running match's data.json through Cloudflare shows the short max-age and a fresh age after each upload

Evals data lives in its own bucket, never in ArchiveBucket: the archive bucket blocks public policy and its bucket-wide lifecycle moves objects to cheaper tiers at 30 and 90 days, while cleanup.py deletes only under archives/
infra/template.yaml shows a separate evals bucket with its own public-read policy scoped to the evals prefix and no lifecycle rule that deletes or tiers published evals
The match host uploads with a dedicated credential that can only put and delete objects under the evals prefix; it is not the deploy identity (issue #39 notes deploys still run as account root)
An attempt with the match-host credential to write outside the evals prefix, or to any other bucket, is denied

A player seat never has a way to read the live site: harness seats run with tools and network off, and a pi-driven Nemotron seat runs pi with --no-tools and --no-mcp; publishing team chat and reasoning live is only allowed for matches where every seat meets this
The harness records each seat's tool and network setting in the match config, and the exporter refuses to publish private content live for a match where any seat has tools on

The pi + Nemotron tester agent never changes public standings: its matches are unrated and hidden from the leaderboard (ratings ledger record_match), or it runs against a local site serve; its runs count against MaxConcurrentMatches only when explicitly allowed
After a tester run, the public leaderboard and every rated player's Elo are unchanged
The match host uploads a turn's thinking files first and its data.json last, so a reader never sees a turn whose reasoning files are not yet there; a missing file still renders as not published
A test that reads between the two upload steps never finds data.json referencing a thinking file that is absent
The live badge goes stale honestly: if a running match's data has not changed for 60 minutes (about twice the slowest turn), the page says no update since HH:MM UTC instead of Live
With a mocked data.json whose generated time is 2 hours old and status running, the page shows the no-update message, not Live

A tested unpublish path exists: delete the object from the evals bucket, purge it from Cloudflare, and confirm a 404 through the public URL, written up as a runbook beside the existing cache-purge section
The runbook is exercised once on a test object and the 404 is recorded

Polling is cheap: the page polls a small per-eval manifest (latest turn, generated time, per-match ETag) and downloads a match's data only when it changed; each match has its own file instead of the prototype's single 2.4 MB bundle of all matches
A viewer idle at the latest turn for 10 minutes downloads under 50 KB when no turn lands
The page reads the data schema version and shows a clear message for a version it does not support, since the page ships with the Lambda package and the data ships separately from the match host
Serving data with a future major version shows the unsupported-version message and no broken board

Streaming stays within static files: while a seat is answering, the match host writes that seat's in-progress thinking and response to a per-seat file every 10 s or so, scanned before each upload; the page polls it every 10 s only while a turn is in progress and the viewer is at the latest turn, and drops it when the turn resolves. Claude seats stream their response text only, since claude -p returns no thinking

During a live turn, a viewer at the latest turn sees a GLM seat's thinking grow within about 10 s of it being generated, a viewer scrubbed back gets no in-progress polling, and a chunk that fails the scanner is never uploaded

tasks.summary: Evals data schema: league_site/evals/schema.py defines the versioned per-match file (state, per-side fog, plans, messages, actions, rejected, latency, think, slices, metrics, structured status+reason, per-seat tool/network setting), the per-eval manifest, thinking and in-progress seat files
acceptance_criteria: pytest: the prototype data.json, converted per match, validates; a file missing status or reason fails validation
pytest: schema exposes a major version and a function that says whether a version is supported
t1 alone creates league_site/evals/__init__.py; t2 and t9 add their modules without touching it

tasks.summary: Free-text scanner: league_site/evals/scan.py classifies reasoning and chat text as clean or not (secret-like strings, hostnames, IPv4/IPv6, absolute paths, emails), failing closed and reporting file, seat and pattern
acceptance_criteria: pytest: planted API key, hostname, private IP, home path and email inside text are each caught; ordinary game text with coordinates like [10,8] passes
pytest: an exception or unknown input type is treated as not clean
a scan report over the 45 prototype thinking files is produced and attached to the PR, listing every hit

tasks.summary: Slicer: league_site/evals/slicer.py turns a match's turns into key-moment slices and templated headlines, plus per-match findings that cite their turns
acceptance_criteria: pytest: hard-a yields slices at turns 17, 18 and 23 with the expected headlines and score deltas
pytest: running the slicer twice on the same input gives identical output; no model client is imported
pytest: every finding carries the turn that backs it

tasks.summary: Benchmark metrics: league_site/evals/metrics.py computes per side per match chat words per turn, median answer time, illegal-order rate, thinking tokens, share of unit-turns in the enemy half, contact within 2 cells, points per turn, order mix and thinking tokens per turn, each with a one-line definition
acceptance_criteria: pytest: values for thief-a4 match a hand-checked fixture (e.g. GLM 1 rejected of 144, Sonnet 16 of 144)
pytest: every metric exposes its definition string, and nothing reads outside the match data

tasks.summary: Exporter: league_site/evals/export.py folds .league/matches/<id> logs and match config into per-match files, manifest and thinking files; runs the scanner and drops failing files only; embeds slices and metrics; refuses to publish private content live for a match where any seat has tools or network on
acceptance_criteria: pytest: a fixture match exports files that validate against the schema; a thinking file with a planted hostname is left out while the turn still exports
pytest: a config with a tools-on seat exports boards and scores but no live chat, plans or reasoning
pytest: the manifest is under 5 KB for six matches and carries per-match ETags
the exporter reads only exported match files; no engine or harness module is imported

tasks.summary: Infra: a dedicated evals bucket in infra/template.yaml with public read only under the evals prefix and no lifecycle rule that deletes or tiers it, plus a match-host IAM user/policy (new infra/iam-match-host-policy.json) limited to put/delete under that prefix
acceptance_criteria: pytest template test: the evals bucket is separate from ArchiveBucket, its policy grants public GetObject only on the evals prefix, and it has no expiring lifecycle
pytest: the match-host policy allows only s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject on the evals prefix

tasks.summary: Cloudflare: route /evals/data/* to the evals bucket on the same domain with cache rules (running match files max-age 30 s or less, finished files immutable), and add an unpublish runbook (delete, purge, confirm 404) to docs/runbooks/cloudflare-league-of-agents-ai.md
acceptance_criteria: curl -I through Cloudflare on a test object shows the expected cache headers and a fresh age after re-upload
the unpublish runbook is exercised once on a test object and the 404 is recorded in the PR

tasks.summary: Publisher: league-site evals publish (CLI under league_site/cli) uploads with the match-host credential: thinking files first, data and manifest last, with cache headers; a --stream mode uploads each answering seat's in-progress thinking and response about every 10 s after scanning each chunk
acceptance_criteria: pytest with a fake S3: upload order is thinking, then match file, then manifest; a reader between steps never sees a missing referenced file
pytest: a chunk that fails the scanner is never uploaded; cache headers are set per file type
dry-run is the default and prints the upload plan as JSON, per the CLI conventions

tasks.summary: Evals styles: league_site/evals/styles.py builds the page CSS from theme.py tokens only, with the validated team colours (light #2b54c4/#b4314f, dark #6f8be6/#e0627f) added as tokens in league_site/web/theme.py
acceptance_criteria: pytest: evals CSS contains no raw hex values outside the token block
the dataviz palette validator passes for the team colours in light and dark; output attached to the PR

tasks.summary: Evals routes: league_site/evals/wsgi.py serves /evals/ and /evals/<eval>/<match>/ inside the site shell and mounts into the site app
acceptance_criteria: pytest: both routes return 200 with the shell, labelled controls and a noscript note; unknown ids return 404
t10 creates league_site/evals/replay_js.py and charts_js.py as stub constants already wired into the page, so t11 and t12 each edit only their own file

tasks.summary: Replay script: league_site/evals/replay_js.py renders the sticky board, the slice story beside it, the open moment (seats, orders, chat, reasoning on demand), the asymmetry note, live polling of the manifest, in-progress streaming, the stale badge and the schema-version guard
acceptance_criteria: node harness: an at-end viewer advances when the manifest gains a turn, a scrubbed viewer does not; in-progress files are polled only at the latest turn during a live turn
node harness: status running with data 2 h old shows the no-update message; an unsupported schema version shows the version message
node harness: a Claude seat shows the claude -p note and a GLM seat loads reasoning text

tasks.summary: Benchmarks script: league_site/evals/charts_js.py renders the index benchmarks (tiles, aggression vs effectiveness, order mix, per-match small multiples, thinking per turn) from exported metrics, with tooltips, keyboard access, table views and each metric's definition
acceptance_criteria: node harness: each chart has a table view whose numbers equal the exported metrics
node harness: tooltip text is set with textContent and every mark has a hit target of at least 24 px

tasks.summary: Playwright suite for /evals/ in tests/e2e plus a CI job: 1440 and 390 px in light and dark, keyboard turn stepping, labelled controls, live advance with a mocked manifest, reasoning loaded on demand; screenshots saved as evidence
acceptance_criteria: CI runs the suite against a local site serve with fixture data and it passes
screenshots at both widths and both themes land in docs/design/evidence/

tasks.summary: pi + Nemotron tester: scripts/pi-tester.sh runs pi on lobes 'worker' (Nemotron 3.5 Super) against a local site serve to exercise /evals/ and the agent onboarding and play flows, plus read-only checks of production /evals/; the run log is kept as evidence
acceptance_criteria: the run completes and its log is committed under docs/verification/; production ratings and leaderboard are unchanged (before/after diff)

tasks.summary: Engine brief: file an issue on agentculture/league-of-agents (communicate skill) for in-progress reasoning and response output per seat, per-seat tool and network settings in match config, and a pi command driver for Nemotron run with --no-tools --no-mcp
acceptance_criteria: the issue exists, cites this spec, and lists the three asks with acceptance criteria

tasks.summary: Verify and ship: deploy, smoke-test /evals/ during a running match, run the two cold reads of hard-a, the evaluator and visitor hallway check, keep the prototype before-screenshot, bump the version and CHANGELOG
acceptance_criteria: production /evals/ shows a live match advancing and streaming reasoning, recorded in the PR
two cold readers both name hard-a turns 17, 18 and 23; answers recorded
version bumped and CHANGELOG entry added

risks.text: Wave 0 has three tasks creating modules in the new league_site/evals package; only t1 may create __init__.py, or the merges collide

The pi tester and the live streaming depend on engine-repo work (issue from t15): in-progress seat output and per-seat tool settings; if it lands late, t8's --stream mode and t5's tools check run against fixtures only
Whether pi's print mode returns Nemotron's full reasoning text through the lobes gateway is unverified; t14 records what it actually gets
The Cloudflare origin rule to an S3 bucket may need a Worker if the plan tier lacks origin rules; t7 decides and records which
